title: LETTER 9: Letter from Customer — Complaint About Unauthorised Transaction

blocks.content: Topic: Write a letter to the HDFC Bank Branch Manager complaining about an unauthorised transaction of Rs. 15,000 in your account and requesting immediate reversal.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Customer complaints regarding unauthorized transactions require immediate formal notification to the bank.
Crucial transaction details such as account number, transaction date, time, and amount must be clearly specified.
Timely reporting is essential to limit customer liability under standard banking guidelines and initiate swift fraud investigation.

blocks.content: Letter from Customer — Complaint About Unauthorised Transaction
Subject: Complaint Regarding Unauthorised Transaction — Request for Immediate Reversal and Investigation

I am Suresh Iyer, a Savings Account holder with your branch (Account No. HDFC-50100XXXXXXXX) since 2016. I write to register a formal complaint regarding a fraudulent debit transaction that has occurred in my account without my authorisation.

On 3 March 2025, at 11:47 PM, I received an SMS alert from the bank notifying me of a debit of Rs. 15,000 through internet banking. I wish to state categorically that I neither initiated nor authorised this transaction. I did not share my internet banking credentials, OTP, or debit card details with anyone. Nor did I receive any OTP on my registered mobile number preceding this transaction, which raises serious questions about the security of my account.

I immediately called the HDFC Bank 24x7 helpline (1800-XXX-XXXX) and reported the fraud at 11:52 PM — within five minutes of receiving the alert. I was given a complaint reference number (HDFC-FRAUD-2025-112233). I have also preserved the SMS alert and the call recording for reference.

As per the Reserve Bank of India's circular on 'Customer Protection — Limiting Liability of Customers in Unauthorised Electronic Banking Transactions,' since I reported the fraud within three working days of receiving notification, and the transaction occurred without any negligence on my part, I am entitled to full reversal of the debited amount.

I request you to kindly investigate this matter on priority, reverse the debited amount of Rs. 15,000 to my account immediately, and take necessary steps to secure my account. I also request a written explanation of how this transaction could have occurred without an OTP being delivered to my registered mobile number.

items: In formal banking correspondence questions, ensure account details and transaction timestamps are explicitly stated.
Always request immediate blocking of compromised cards or net banking access to demonstrate urgency in letter writing format.
Maintain a formal, precise, and polite tone while clearly asserting the demand for account safety and restitution.

blocks.content: Examiner's Tip: In fraud complaint letters, cite the specific RBI circular on customer liability to show awareness of your legal rights. Always mention complaint reference numbers, timings, and exactly what steps you took. This creates a legally sound record.
